title: Connector Twin: know what your agent did, see what it saw, undo what it changed
one_line: A service that journals every request and response an AI agent makes through a connector such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive or Slack, and replays that journal into the views the agent saw, with a before and after for every change and a revert plan for each one.
question: Do you know what your agents did?

policy.without: The scopes you granted, if anybody wrote them down.
policy.with: The same scopes, plus the list of actions they allow that cannot be undone, such as a permanent delete or a sent email.

policy.without: The agent's own summary, and administrator audit logs that record that events changed.
policy.with: Every call, with the request and the response, in order, hash-chained so a missing or edited entry shows.

policy.without: Nothing. The inbox has moved on since.
policy.with: The inbox and the calendar as the agent saw them at each step, rebuilt from the responses it received.

policy.without: Nothing, unless the chat was kept.
policy.with: The instruction that led to each call, when prompt capture is on.

policy.without: Deletes to trash, yes, for 30 days. Edits, sent email and notifications, no. A permanent delete, only by an administrator's bulk restore within 25 days.
policy.with: A revert plan for every change, and a named list of what cannot be undone and why.
An evidence chain that an auditor, an insurer or a board can open with a read key.

setup.name: Connector review, small
setup.includes: Irreversibility map of the scopes in use, capture set up in one mode, a first behaviour-policy baseline.

setup.name: Connector review, team
setup.includes: As above, plus retention rules, key custody set up with the customer, and a replay drill on a real session.

setup.name: Connector review, organisation
setup.includes: As above, plus the customer-cloud deployment, the broker in front of the connectors, and an incident runbook.

monthly.name: Journal
monthly.includes: Capture of every request and response, encrypted retention for 90 days, search, chain verification.

monthly.name: Twin
monthly.includes: Journal, plus the rebuilt views, before and after for every change, revert plans, and 1 year of retention.

monthly.name: Assured
monthly.includes: Twin, plus a monthly evidence pack for the behaviour policy and the insurer, two incident replays a year, retention to 7 years, keys held by the customer.

on_demand.name: Incident replay
on_demand.includes: A day's investigation: what the agent saw, what it did, what it said it did, and what can be put back.

on_demand.name: Supervised revert
on_demand.includes: Executing the revert plan with the customer watching, and recording the result in the journal.

packages.note: Every price is a hypothesis to test with the first ten customers, not a measured result.

modes.name: Broker
modes.where: A service between the agent and the connector holds the credentials and makes the calls.
modes.evidence: Strongest: nothing reaches the API without passing through it. This is the execution broker described on twins.sgit.ai.
modes.trade: The broker holds credentials and sees traffic in flight, so it is the highest-value target in the estate.

modes.name: Gateway
modes.where: A proxy on the MCP or HTTP path records calls but the agent keeps its own credentials.
modes.evidence: Strong for anything routed through it; blind to any path around it.
modes.trade: Easier to deploy; needs the routing enforced.

modes.name: Agent-reported
modes.where: The agent is told to append a copy of every request and response it sends.
modes.evidence: Weakest: an agent that omits an entry leaves a gap the chain cannot show. Marked as self-reported in the policy.
modes.trade: Available today with no infrastructure at all.

assumptions: An active assistant agent makes about 500 connector calls a day, and a call with its response averages about 20 KB of JSON. That is about 10 MB a day, or 0.3 GB a month, per agent.
Object storage costs about 0.02 USD per GB per month. A year of retention for one agent is about 3.6 GB, well under 0.10 USD a month.
Broker and processor compute is estimated at 3 GBP per agent per month at small scale, so infrastructure is about 3.10 GBP per agent per month including storage.
Two founders at 6,000 GBP a month each fully loaded, plus 2,000 GBP a month of tooling, is a monthly burn of 14,000 GBP.
economics.break_even: At the Twin price of 40 GBP per agent, less about 3.10 GBP of infrastructure, break-even on that burn is about 380 agents: roughly 38 customers with ten agents each.
